s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 70s
The patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
The patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
The rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
The rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
The patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with the onset of the rash
A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Biopsy findings showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

raw.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy

The patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
The rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
The rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs

A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Biopsy findings showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

differentials: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome
per_call: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome

raw.rationale: The rash started 2 months after initiation of pembrolizumab, a known cause of immune-related adverse events including skin reactions, and the biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils are consistent with an immune-mediated reaction.

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: While ipilimumab can also cause skin reactions, the temporal relationship and biopsy findings do not specifically point to ipilimumab over pembrolizumab as the culprit

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: The presence of eosinophils is noted, but the clinical presentation and biopsy findings are more suggestive of a drug-induced rash than eosinophilic cellulitis

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: The description of the rash as erythematous annular plaques could fit erythema annulare centrifugum, but the context of recent immunotherapy initiation makes a drug-induced rash more likely

rejected.label: Fixed drug eruption
rejected.why: The rash did not present as a fixed, well-defined lesion and the lack of response to terbinafine does not support a fungal etiology, making fixed drug eruption less likely
